column3: The Greek has singular “heart” rather than plural “hearts.”
The passive “was raised” is rendered “has risen.”
“The two” and “Jesus” make the subjects and referent explicit; the passive recognition is made active.
BSB’s “Jesus” matches the Textus Receptus (Ἰησοῦς); the critical text has no name. “Says” is rendered in the past tense.
The Greek describes their thinking they were seeing a spirit, rather than had seen one.
“Jesus” supplies the subject; singular “heart” becomes plural “hearts.”
“His” is supplied before hands and feet.
“Jesus” supplies the subject. BSB lacks “My” before words, as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text has it (μου).
BSB’s “and forgiveness” matches the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “for forgiveness” (εἰς). The Greek participle “beginning” refers to the people addressed.
